entities.summary:
Perictione was the mother of the Greek philosopher Plato, born to an aristocratic Athenian family in ancient Greece around 470 BCE. Her husband, Sophroniscus, was also a prominent figure in Athens, and their son Plato went on to found the Academy, one of the earliest institutions of higher learning in the Western world.

Perictione's life is not well-documented, but it is known that she played an important role as a mother and a matriarch within her family. As such, her influence extended beyond her immediate family to shape the intellectual and cultural heritage of ancient Greece.

Despite the lack of detailed information about Perictione's personal life, her legacy can be seen in the enduring impact of her son Plato's philosophical ideas on Western thought.

The legacy of Perictione extends not only through her famous son but also through the cultural and intellectual traditions of ancient Greece more broadly.
